messages.subject: Constraining range states at the corners
messages.subject_clean: Constraining range states at the corners
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I was running Time stratified Biogeobears analysis on a dataset of 357 tips. I provided the areas allowed matrix. But despite that, the "corner nodes" which represent the immediate geographic ranges after cladogenesis were displaying odd areas. Is there any way to constrain the "corner nodes" to specific areas?

Thanks in advance.

messages.body_plain:
On Friday, June 19, 2020 at 3:35:27 PM UTC+12, mahi bansal wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I was running Time stratified Biogeobears analysis on a dataset of 357 tips. I provided the areas allowed matrix. But despite that, the "corner nodes" which represent the immediate geographic ranges after cladogenesis were displaying odd areas. Is there any way to constrain the "corner nodes" to specific areas?
>
> Thanks in advance.

Hi -- this is probably an example of this issue:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#Most_prob_states_not_joint

The manual states list is a better method than the areas allowed matrix for anything except the simplest case (islands sinking back in time):
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#areas_allowed_matrix2
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#manual_modify_states

Re: constraining the "corner" nodes - it is theoretically possible, but programming it would be a major project. An approach that might help, if you have some justification (e.g. a fossil), would be to insert a fossil as a side-branch with a branch length of e.g. 0.0000001 just above the corner in question.  But I would try the above approaches first!

Cheers,
Nick
